full_judgment:
4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 3, government contested the suit contending that the suit filed by the plaintiffs is not maintainable, barred by limitation, estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. That the 1st schedule land of the plaint is the khas land of the Government and as such, S.A. record has rightly been prepared the name of the Government as গোপাট type of land. That the 1st schedule land of the plaint is being used by the local people as a গোপাট and the aforesaid 1st schedule land is the only way of the local people through which they go to the nearest Haor. That the plaintiffs and proforma defendants have or had no right, title and interest in the 1" schedule land of the plaint. And they are trying to grab the 1st schedule land and as such, on behalf of the local people one Kazi Mokbul Hossain filed an application before the defendants for demarcating and separating the same from the 2nd schedule land of the plaint. That on 06.05.1998 a date was fixed for demarcation of the same but due to non-cooperation of the plaintiffs the date was shifted and on 20.05.1998 it was fixed for demarcation but the plaintiff created obstruction hence the 1st schedule land of the plaint has not yet been demarcated. The defendants therefore, prayed the suit to be dismissed. 

 10. Mrs. Samira Tarannum Rabeya, the learned Deputy Attorney General, has submitted that the learned additional district judge having came to the finding on a consideration of the evidence and the circumstances of the case that the 1st schedule land of the plaint is the khas land of the government and as such S.A record had rightly prepared in the name of the government as গোপাট type of land. That the schedule of the plaint is being used by the local people as গোপাট and aforesaid 1st schedule land is only way of the local people by which they go to nearest Haor. The plaintiffs and proforma defendants have or had no right title and interest in the 1st schedule land of the pliant. The land in question, as she submits, as it would borne by the evidence on record and was exhibited and reflected in the report of the inquiry commission, is not only a government land but a khal treating the same, as khas land and the high Court Division ought to have considered in its findings and decision upon adverting the same and thus occasioned an error of law causing failure of justice.
